lines.text: What looked like an interior can be arranged as a succession. The count does not fall with its visibility.
One, five, twenty-one: one more has acquired a different cost.
Equal counts have bought different bodies. Where would you spend the next split?
The chair was not simply waiting inside the cube. Its discarded cells make the choice visible.
A trunk waits. Each fork inherits a direction and a length; two descendants give 31 segments, three give 121.
Follow a fork to its last visible branch. Colour, bounds and endpoints reveal the same fixed-seed sculpture.
One bar is waiting. More pieces can leave less material: separate the latest cut from its visible history.
A gap for whom? Give the intervals thickness, then test which openings admit the body.
Four metres between the endpoints; more than twelve along the line. Where did the detour go?
The removed middles become the work. Which part of the same operation receives a body?
The points stay put while the fitted slope moves. What belongs to the shape, and what belongs to this reading?

lines.note: Zero volume depends on iterating without end, and the 20 that makes the sponge 2.727-dimensional is the same 20 that prices the next tick — 20, 400, 8,000 bodies, then 160,000 — so D = log(20)/log(3) is also the invoice.

note_src.quote: each Menger tick multiplies the cube count by 20, so once/coarse/fine are 20/400/8000 bodies and a fourth rung would be 160,000 ... D = log(20)/log(3) is exactly why this ladder stops early

lines.text: The Menger sponge has infinite surface area and zero volume
Recursive mathematical sequences and spiral visualizations
lines.note: Phyllotaxis depends on phi resisting every rational approximation, and the float holding it is a rational — so the seed head that must never repeat is laid out from a number that already does.

note_src.quote: The golden ratio is the most irrational number — its continued fraction is all 1s, making it the slowest to converge and the hardest to approximate by rationals.

lines.note: A boundary is where the orbit neither settles nor escapes, and this floor decides in 200 iterations after 50 of warmup — so its black calligraphy is not a curve but the pixels the cutoff could not resolve.

note_src.quote: Stable (λ<0) = blue, chaotic (λ>0) = yellow/red, boundary (λ≈0) = black.

lines.note: Never ending depends on a zoom with no floor, and the header promises copies of yourself at 10^15 while the slider stops at 10^6 with escape decided inside 500 iterations — the infinite regress ends in a constant.

note_src.quote: critical_parameter: Zoom depth. At 10x you see the cardioid. At 10000x you see seahorses. At 10^15 you see copies of yourself.

pearls.edge: Two recursions with no base case depend on a stopping condition neither side owns, so the chamber borrows the learner's body — walking out is the room's only termination, and quitting has to be read as the answer.

edge_src.quote: The chamber ends when the learner chooses to leave, and the choice is itself part of the chamber's argument

lines.text: A cloud is not a thing — it is a threshold. The same noise field with different cutoff is sky
lines.note: A cloud is only a cutoff, and this cutoff is asked 32 times per axis across twenty metres — one question every 0.625 m, five octaves — so the gallery of all scales owns the five it can afford.

note_src.quote: A cloud is not a thing — it is a threshold. The same noise field with different cutoff is sky, cloud, or fog. Only the cutoff decides.

lines.note: Filling every point without crossing depends on the drawing still reading as a line, and one rung past standard the 3-pixel stroke closes its own gaps into a solid block — the curve disappears exactly when it succeeds.

note_src.quote: At `fine` the cells get small enough that a 3px stroke closes the gaps and the curve reads as a filled block, so it thins to 1.
